cross-cutting.title: 14 of 39 apps had no git remote (9) or no git at all (5) and 7 live Workers had no local source, so one disk loss destroys them
cross-cutting.symptom: A portfolio deploy sweep found kindly, patentcake, payrails, paystudy and pitchdecks with no repo, ABS, evertrue, gitbagel, joy, skillsea, traderjournal, birthdaytreat and two marketing repos with no remote, and hopefil, coconvo-ai, listing-lab, listing-lab-pro, social-levelup and two safe-haven Workers deployed with no source on this machine.
cross-cutting.fix: Inventory script (dirs x git status x ahead/behind x workers_list) surfaced them; owner chose to import the orphans into GitBagel and an importer was written, but it needs the owner's gb_session. Recommend a remote for every deployed Worker.

cross-cutting.title: Background work dropped because it wasn't passed to ctx.waitUntil()
cross-cutting.symptom: Analytics writes, audit logs, cache warms, or D1 upserts kicked off right before returning a Response land only sometimes; they silently vanish under real traffic with no error.
cross-cutting.fix: Pass any post-response work to ctx.waitUntil(promise) so the runtime keeps it alive after the response is sent; await it instead if the client must see the result. Never leave a floating promise expecting it to finish on its own.

cross-cutting.title: Bulk import silently drops rows it can't parse
cross-cutting.symptom: A user uploads 200 leads; 170 land, 30 vanish with no message. The loss is invisible until a customer can't be found weeks later.
cross-cutting.fix: Count input rows, count inserts, and after import show 'N imported, M skipped, K duplicates' with a downloadable list of the exact skipped rows and why. Never discard an unparseable row silently.

cross-cutting.title: Data export silently omits notes, activity history and timeline
cross-cutting.symptom: Users export 'all my data' to leave or back up and get only the contact/lead rows — call notes, emails, meeting history and timeline events are missing, discovered only after the old tool is gone.
cross-cutting.fix: Export the full object graph, not just top-level rows: include notes, communications, activity/timeline, attachments and payment history in one archive. Show a per-table row count so users can verify completeness.

cross-cutting.title: Disk full (ENOSPC) mid-session silently drops Edit/Write results and blanket cleanup deletes other sessions' tool outputs
cross-cutting.symptom: A multi-line edit errored with ENOSPC; after freeing space the file had 0 matches for the new view so the work looked done but was not. An attempted cleanup `rm -rf .../tasks/*.output` removed concurrent sessions' output files; wiping ~/.npm/_cacache later forced npx to re-resolve wrangler and broke a deploy.
cross-cutting.fix: After any ENOSPC, free space with targeted rebuildable caches (not other sessions' tasks/*.output or npm's whole cache), then re-verify every pending edit with grep -c and re-apply; check df -h / at the start of long or parallel runs and reclaim before big multi-agent jobs.

cross-cutting.title: Export is partial or lossy — misses media, one item at a time, or PDF-only
cross-cutting.symptom: Users trying to leave or back up find the export omits photos/attachments/voice notes, only exports a single entry at a time, or dumps to a flat PDF that can't be re-imported.
cross-cutting.fix: Ship a one-click 'export everything' that bundles all record types plus their media into an open, re-importable archive (JSON/NDJSON + attachments in a zip). Verify a round-trip re-import. Include derived content (comments, milestones, generated docs), not just raw notes.

cross-cutting.title: Portfolio scan 2026-10-04: image/upload inputs with no size/type guard (IMG-DROP) on 13 apps
cross-cutting.symptom: File/image inputs accept any type and size with no client-side guard — risks silent oversize failures (data-loss) and billable storage DoS.
cross-cutting.fix: Validate type and cap size client-side with a clear error, and enforce the same limits server-side before writing to R2.

cross-cutting.title: Uncaught QuotaExceededError when writing large blobs to localStorage
cross-cutting.symptom: Saving images/base64/large JSON to localStorage throws QuotaExceededError past ~5MB; the write is swallowed so the user's data silently isn't persisted, or the whole save handler crashes.
cross-cutting.fix: Wrap writes in try/catch and handle QuotaExceededError explicitly (evict, or surface a clear message). Move anything large or binary to IndexedDB; keep localStorage for small primitives only. Cap/prune cached payloads and never dump media into it.

cross-cutting.title: Unsynced in-memory state wiped on refresh, tab-close, or crash
cross-cutting.symptom: Everything the user typed since opening the app is gone after a refresh, an accidental close, or a background-tab eviction.
cross-cutting.fix: Autosave to local storage on every meaningful change (debounced), rehydrate on boot, and treat the server as a sync target, not the only store. Add a beforeunload flush for anything still pending.

cross-cutting.title: D1 'too many SQL variables' — 100 bound-parameter limit, not 999
cross-cutting.symptom: Bulk insert/update or a WHERE ... IN (?, ?, ...) over a dynamic array throws 'D1_ERROR: too many SQL variables at offset N'; works with a few rows in dev, blows up on real data.
cross-cutting.fix: Chunk writes so (rows x columns) stays under 100 placeholders per statement and run the chunks with db.batch([...]) in a single transaction; for large IN() lists, chunk the array or join against a temp/values table.

cross-cutting.title: Happy-path assumption — no null/undefined guards
cross-cutting.symptom: AI code assumes API/optional data is always present and dereferences it, crashing on the empty/error case.
cross-cutting.fix: Guard every optional/awaited value before use; handle the empty and error branches explicitly.

cross-cutting.title: typeof does not guard a let/const in its temporal dead zone
cross-cutting.symptom: A defensive `typeof x` guard still threw ReferenceError at runtime.
cross-cutting.fix: Guard with a try/catch, or move the reference after the declaration / hoist a `var` sentinel.

cross-cutting.title: White-screen ChunkLoadError after deploy from SPA index.html fallback
cross-cutting.symptom: Users with the tab already open (or a stale service worker) get a blank page or 'ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk failed' after a deploy; a hard refresh fixes it, so it looks intermittent.
cross-cutting.fix: Make asset paths (extensions like .js/.css) return a real 404 instead of the SPA fallback; serve index.html with no-cache and hashed assets with immutable long cache. Add an inline recovery script that catches failed dynamic imports, unregisters service workers, and does a one-time hard reload.

cross-cutting.title: Accounts exist with no delete-my-data path
cross-cutting.symptom: A user asks to be deleted and there is no mechanism — deleting the app leaves everything on the server.
cross-cutting.fix: Ship a one-tap 'delete my account and data' that genuinely purges server records and backups, and state honestly what it cannot reach (e.g. immutable audit logs). A GDPR right and an app-store requirement. Detector: PRIV-NO-DELETE.

cross-cutting.title: Collects personal data with no privacy policy
cross-cutting.symptom: The product takes an email, name or phone number and there is no policy anywhere saying what happens to it.
cross-cutting.fix: Publish a privacy policy stating what you collect, why, the legal basis, how long you keep it and how to delete it. Required under UK/EU GDPR and by both app stores. Detector: PRIV-NO-POLICY.

cross-cutting.title: Consent banner that is non-compliant or purely decorative
cross-cutting.symptom: Non-essential cookies/trackers load before any consent is given, or the banner offers 'Accept all' with no equally easy 'Reject all'.
cross-cutting.fix: Load no non-essential tracker until consent is recorded; make reject as prominent and as few clicks as accept; store and honour the choice; nothing pre-ticked.

cross-cutting.title: Data kept indefinitely with no retention policy
cross-cutting.symptom: Every record ever created is still stored, including data for deleted or long-dormant accounts.
cross-cutting.fix: Define and document a retention period per data class, delete or anonymise past it on a schedule, and state the periods in the privacy policy. GDPR storage limitation requires it.

cross-cutting.title: Personal data or credentials written to logs
cross-cutting.symptom: Emails, passwords, tokens or entire user records land in the console and in retained server logs.
cross-cutting.fix: Log identifiers, never payloads. Redact known-sensitive keys centrally in the logging helper so it cannot be forgotten at a call site. Detector: PRIV-PII-LOG.

cross-cutting.title: Personal data placed in a URL query string
cross-cutting.symptom: Emails, tokens or identifiers appear in links, and therefore in server logs, browser history, bookmarks and outbound Referer headers.
cross-cutting.fix: Never put personal data or secrets in a URL. Use a POST body or an opaque short-lived id, and set an appropriate Referrer-Policy. Detector: PRIV-PII-IN-URL.

cross-cutting.title: Portfolio scan 2026-10-04: 14 apps have no delete-my-data path, 13 have no privacy policy
cross-cutting.symptom: PRIV-NO-DELETE on 14/23 apps and PRIV-NO-POLICY on 13/23 — accounts with no self-serve data deletion and no privacy policy.
cross-cutting.fix: Add a one-tap 'delete my account & data' that purges D1/KV/R2, plus a short privacy policy, to every app that stores user data; state honestly what deletion cannot reach.

cross-cutting.title: Sensitive data routed through third-party ad/analytics SDKs
cross-cutting.symptom: Health, reproductive, financial or precise-location data is transmitted to advertising or analytics platforms as a side effect of a routine SDK.
cross-cutting.fix: Classify sensitive data explicitly; keep it on-device or end-to-end encrypted; never let it reach third-party ad/analytics/attribution SDKs; gate any tracker behind explicit consent and offer a local-only mode. A jury held a major platform liable in 2025 for exactly this pattern. Detector: PRIV-3P-TRACKER.

cross-cutting.title: User-to-user apps are in UK Online Safety Act scope with no risk assessment or report path
cross-cutting.symptom: BirthdayTreat, GitBagel, Stepapa, Stitchhooky, the Finished. feed and the Hallalu portal are user-to-user services in scope of the OSA. None has an illegal-content risk assessment, a documented reporting/takedown route or an Ofcom-checker record.
cross-cutting.fix: Open: run Ofcom's regulation checker per app, write a short illegal-content risk assessment, and add a report/takedown route and contact. Enforcement so far has hit non-responders and harmful sites, with no micro-service fined.

cross-cutting.title: Failed save/sync silently drops the user's edit (no offline write queue)
cross-cutting.symptom: User adds/edits an entry while offline or on a flaky connection; the network call fails and the change just vanishes with no error and no retry. Widely reported (offline sync halting mid-way; habit/journal users losing entries in tunnels/planes).
cross-cutting.fix: Local-first: persist every write to IndexedDB/local storage first, render from local, then flush a durable outbox to the server with retry + backoff. Never discard a local write because the remote call failed; surface a 'pending sync' state instead of dropping data.

cross-cutting.title: KV read-after-write returns stale value (eventual consistency)
cross-cutting.symptom: Code writes a value to Workers KV then reads it back in the same or next request and gets the OLD value (or a cached 'key does not exist' for a just-created key); UI shows stale data for up to ~60s and 'saves that didn't save' reports follow.
cross-cutting.fix: Never rely on immediate read-after-write from KV. Return the just-written value from memory instead of re-reading; put anything needing read-your-writes (sessions, counters, dedupe) in D1 or a Durable Object; only use KV for read-mostly config/assets.

cross-cutting.title: wrangler deploy from a shared worktree shipped another session's committed but unfinished feature
cross-cutting.symptom: A deploy for a small fix also published a half-built Speak feature that a concurrent session had just committed, and an auto-commit swept the fix into that session's commit.
cross-cutting.fix: Check git status and git log for other sessions' changes before deploy, deploy from a clean worktree of your own commit, and stage only the files you touched.

cross-cutting.title: Cache-overwrite race in AI/caching layer corrupts entries
cross-cutting.symptom: Under concurrent requests, a cached AI response or computed value gets served for the WRONG input key; passes every test because tests run sequentially, fails only under parallel load.
cross-cutting.fix: Key the cache strictly by a hash of the full input and write atomically (no shared 'current' slot); dedupe in-flight identical requests with a promise map; load-test concurrently before merging anything touching caching.

cross-cutting.title: Floating promises / unhandled async errors
cross-cutting.symptom: Promises not awaited or lacking catch, so failures are silent and ordering is wrong.
cross-cutting.fix: Await or .catch every promise; surface async errors; avoid fire-and-forget for state changes.

cross-cutting.title: Hard-coded environment-specific values
cross-cutting.symptom: localhost URLs, absolute paths, ports or keys baked in that break outside the author's machine.
cross-cutting.fix: Read config from env; no machine-specific literals in shipped code.

cross-cutting.title: No error handling on network calls
cross-cutting.symptom: fetch/HTTP calls with no try/catch, timeout or retry, so a blip becomes a broken UI.
cross-cutting.fix: Wrap network calls with try/catch + timeout + a user-visible fallback; retry idempotent reads.

cross-cutting.title: Silent catch swallowing errors
cross-cutting.symptom: catch blocks that do nothing, hiding real failures and making bugs invisible.
cross-cutting.fix: Handle or surface every caught error; never swallow silently.

cross-cutting.title: A fitting theory was recorded as a definitive diagnosis ('Aprizely auto-deploys from GitHub') and acted on, then retracted
cross-cutting.symptom: The session summary stated the git-deploy cause as established and the session committed and pushed on that basis; there is no .github/workflows, no package.json and no CI in the repo. Twenty minutes later: 'my earlier conclusion was wrong'.
cross-cutting.fix: Treat a root cause as a hypothesis until its prediction is tested; do not put it in summaries or memory beforehand. A separate hypothesis (wrangler logged into another Cloudflare account, because deployments list shows a different author email) was ruled out by matching whoami's account id to wrangler.json.

cross-cutting.title: AI-generated fact asserted to users without verification
cross-cutting.symptom: A feature summary, competitor comparison or 'insight' presented to users contains details the model invented.
cross-cutting.fix: Ground generated text strictly in supplied data, instruct the model never to invent, show the source alongside the claim, and fall back to a deterministic local summary when grounding is unavailable.

cross-cutting.title: Apple Color Emoji artwork used as shipped image assets outside Apple's licence
cross-cutting.symptom: Where emoji are exported or shipped as image assets, they use Apple Color Emoji artwork, which is licensed only 'while running the Apple Software' (macOS SLA 2E).
cross-cutting.fix: Open: switch shipped emoji assets to Twemoji (CC-BY 4.0) or Noto Emoji (OFL 1.1) with attribution.

cross-cutting.title: Manufactured scarcity or urgency in the UI
cross-cutting.symptom: The page shows a countdown, 'only 3 left', or 'X people are viewing this' that is not derived from real state.
cross-cutting.fix: Only display scarcity that is literally true and derived from real data. Fabricated urgency is unlawful under UK/EU consumer protection rules and an active enforcement target. Detector: CLAIM-FAKE-SCARCITY.

cross-cutting.title: Placeholder or sample content shipped to real users
cross-cutting.symptom: Lorem ipsum, TODO markers, 'John Doe' testimonials or 'your text here' appear in the live product.
cross-cutting.fix: Sweep for placeholder patterns before every deploy. Note that fabricated testimonials are not just embarrassing — they are unlawful. Detector: CLAIM-PLACEHOLDER.

cross-cutting.title: Several product names shipped without trademark clearance (Evertrue, Kindly, Fullfill, Payrails)
cross-cutting.symptom: Register hits: Evertrue vs EverTrue Inc US Reg. 4613429 (class 9, renewed 2025). Kindly vs Convertelligence AS UK00801403375/UK00801530675 (classes 9/41/42, to 2030). Fullfill vs an identical 'fullfill' UK00004405179 filed 21/06/2026 (also US 99908068). Payrails vs Payrails GmbH US 97082130/97082153 (classes 9/35/36/42, pending).
cross-cutting.fix: Open: rename or narrow the specification (Evertrue UK-only), monitor the pending Fullfill application, and file COCONVO, HALLALU and APRIZELY (clean on GB/EM/US) first.

cross-cutting.title: Statistic published with no citable source
cross-cutting.symptom: A percentage or research-style figure appears in marketing or in-app copy, and no one can say where it came from when challenged.
cross-cutting.fix: Every published number needs a real, checkable primary source recorded next to it; if you cannot cite it, delete it. Detector: CLAIM-UNSOURCED-STAT.

cross-cutting.title: Unverifiable superlative claim shipped in product copy
cross-cutting.symptom: The product asserts it is the 'first', 'only' or 'best' of its kind, and the claim turns out to be untrue when checked against primary sources.
cross-cutting.fix: Verify every superlative against a primary source or soften it to something provable ('built for…', 'designed around…'). Unprovable comparative claims are both a trust problem and an advertising-law risk. Detector: CLAIM-SUPERLATIVE.

cross-cutting.title: Click handler on a div/span — not keyboard reachable
cross-cutting.symptom: A control works with a mouse but cannot be reached or activated by keyboard or screen reader at all.
cross-cutting.fix: Use a real <button>. If impossible, add role="button", tabindex="0" and an explicit Enter/Space keydown handler. Detector: A11Y-CLICK-NONINTERACTIVE.

cross-cutting.title: Document missing a lang attribute
cross-cutting.symptom: Screen readers pronounce the page with the wrong language voice, making content hard or impossible to follow.
cross-cutting.fix: Set <html lang="en"> (or the actual language), and mark inline foreign-language passages with their own lang. Detector: A11Y-NO-LANG.

cross-cutting.title: Drag-only interaction with no single-pointer alternative (WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.7 Dragging Movements)
cross-cutting.symptom: Reorder / move / slider interactions that only work by dragging exclude users who cannot perform a drag (motor impairment, switch access).
cross-cutting.fix: Always pair a drag with a non-drag alternative — Move up/down buttons, a right-click/kebab menu, or number entry — unless dragging is essential.

cross-cutting.title: Focus indicator removed by outline:none
cross-cutting.symptom: Keyboard users tabbing through the interface cannot see where they are — focus becomes invisible.
cross-cutting.fix: Never reset the outline without providing a high-contrast :focus-visible style. WCAG 2.2 requires a visible focus indicator meeting minimum size and contrast. Detector: A11Y-FOCUS-KILLED.

cross-cutting.title: Form field with no associated label
cross-cutting.symptom: A screen reader reaches the input and announces only 'edit text' — the user cannot tell what to type. Affects ~51% of pages and has been a top failure for over five years.
cross-cutting.fix: Give each field an id plus <label for=…>, or an aria-label when a visible label is genuinely impossible. Never rely on placeholder alone. Detector: A11Y-INPUT-NOLABEL.

cross-cutting.title: Icon-only button or link with no accessible name
cross-cutting.symptom: Screen readers announce 'button' or read out the URL; empty links appear on ~46% of pages and empty buttons on ~31%.
cross-cutting.fix: Add aria-label (or visually-hidden text) to every icon-only control; give inline SVGs a <title>. Detector: A11Y-EMPTY-CONTROL.

cross-cutting.title: Images with no alt attribute
cross-cutting.symptom: Screen readers announce the raw filename (or nothing) instead of the image's meaning; present on ~53% of pages.
cross-cutting.fix: Every gets an alt: descriptive text for meaningful images, alt="" for purely decorative ones so it is skipped. Detector: A11Y-IMG-ALT.

cross-cutting.title: Low-contrast text below the 4.5:1 minimum
cross-cutting.symptom: Light grey body text on white is unreadable for low-vision users and in sunlight; appears on ~84% of homepages, the single most common accessibility failure.
cross-cutting.fix: Enforce 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (and for UI/graphical boundaries). Check every token pair in BOTH light and dark themes with a contrast checker, not by eye.

cross-cutting.title: PIN/OTP field blocks paste or uses a cognitive-test CAPTCHA (WCAG 2.2 · 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication)
cross-cutting.symptom: A login/recovery step relies on a cognitive function test (transcribe/solve/recognise) or disables paste into the code field, which WCAG 2.2 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) forbids without an alternative.
cross-cutting.fix: Allow paste and password managers to fill PIN/OTP fields; offer a non-cognitive authentication path; avoid puzzle/transcription CAPTCHAs as the only option.

cross-cutting.title: Positive tabindex breaks the natural tab order
cross-cutting.symptom: Tabbing jumps around the page unpredictably, skipping or reordering controls.
cross-cutting.fix: Use only tabindex="0" (focusable in document order) or "-1" (programmatic focus). Fix ordering by fixing the DOM order. Detector: A11Y-POSITIVE-TABINDEX.

cross-cutting.title: Touch target smaller than 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.8 Target Size)
cross-cutting.symptom: Small icon buttons — a row options dot, a drag handle, an inline ✕, a bell toggle — are hard to hit accurately on touch and fail WCAG 2.2 Target Size (Minimum).
cross-cutting.fix: Give every pointer target at least a 24×24px hit area (padding or min-width/height), or space inline controls so each has 24px of exclusive space. Exceptions: inline-in-text links and equivalent nearby controls.

cross-cutting.title: Empty catch block swallows the error
cross-cutting.symptom: A feature silently does nothing; there is no error in the console and no clue in any log about what failed.
cross-cutting.fix: Never leave a catch empty: log the error with context and surface a user-visible failure state. If the failure genuinely is expected and safe, say so in a comment. Detector: OBS-EMPTY-CATCH.

cross-cutting.title: No build/version stamp to correlate an error with a deploy
cross-cutting.symptom: A bug report cannot be tied to a release, so it is impossible to tell whether a fix shipped or which deploy caused a regression.
cross-cutting.fix: Stamp a build id/version into the app, show it in settings or the console, and attach it to every logged error so failures map to a specific deploy.

cross-cutting.title: No global error handler — front-end crashes are invisible
cross-cutting.symptom: Users report a white screen or a dead button and there is no record anywhere that anything went wrong.
cross-cutting.fix: Register window error and unhandledrejection listeners that log/report with context (route, build version, user id — never personal data). Without them a white screen produces no signal at all. Detector: OBS-NO-ERROR-HANDLER.

cross-cutting.title: Promise chain with no .catch — rejections vanish
cross-cutting.symptom: An async action fails with no visible effect; the UI shows a spinner forever or silently stays unchanged.
cross-cutting.fix: Attach .catch() to every chain (or use try/await), and register a global unhandledrejection handler as a backstop. Detector: OBS-UNHANDLED-PROMISE.

cross-cutting.title: Workers Assets deploys 'succeeded' for 35 minutes while static files stayed stale, and a one-off fresh result was a false positive
cross-cutting.symptom: Eight wrangler deploys printed Success and the deployments list showed the new version at 100%, yet /app.js and /app.css kept serving old content (cf-cache-status HIT, same etag, query-string cache-busting ignored) and a brand-new public/*.txt returned 404. wrangler kept saying 'No updated asset files to upload'.
cross-cutting.fix: Final fix: the worker rewrites asset references in the HTML shell to /_v/<ASSET_VER>/file and serves /_v/* (a wildcard run_worker_first entry) from ASSETS with immutable caching, so each release has a new path. ASSET_VER is bumped by hand each deploy, which is a footgun. Prove deploys with a never-cached version route and by comparing the served file's sha with the local file, not with wrangler's output, and re-check after the next deploy before trusting a fix.

cross-cutting.title: .only() left in a test suite silently skips everything else
cross-cutting.symptom: CI stays green while running a single test; broken code ships because the rest of the suite never executed.
cross-cutting.fix: Remove .only before committing and add a lint or CI rule that fails the build when it appears. Detector: TEST-ONLY.

cross-cutting.title: A 'tsc exit' check written as `| head; echo $?` or `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` always looks clean, and PIPESTATUS is empty under zsh
cross-cutting.symptom: Typecheck lines printed 'tsc: 0' next to a real TS2339 error; the replacement `echo EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` printed a blank exit code that was read as success.
cross-cutting.fix: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` unpiped (or set -o pipefail) and gate on its own exit code; if filtering output, capture to a file first.

cross-cutting.title: A hidden Browser pane gives blank screenshots and timeouts that were mistaken for page defects
cross-cutting.symptom: Screenshots of SkillSea, Hallalu and the finish verification came back blank or timed out with 'pane is not displayed'; a tab pinned to a local file preview refused navigation; the Aprizely board tab kept taking focus.
cross-cutting.fix: When the pane is hidden verify through DOM and text (find, read_page, get_page_text) and say so; open a new tab instead of navigating a pinned one; front the app tab before screenshots.

cross-cutting.title: A syntax-check loop that pipes node --check through head reports ALL OK even when a file is broken
cross-cutting.symptom: `for f in *.js; do node --check "$f" 2>&1 | head -2 || ok=0; done` printed success for every file regardless of syntax errors, so the pre-deploy gate could not fail.
cross-cutting.fix: Drop the pipe (run `node --check "$f" || fail=1`) or use `set -o pipefail`; make the loop exit non-zero and chain commit/deploy with && so a failing check stops the ship.

cross-cutting.title: No tests anywhere in the project
cross-cutting.symptom: Every regression is found by a user; there is no signal before deploy that the core loop still works.
cross-cutting.fix: Add at least a smoke test of the core loop (sign in → create → save → reload and it persists → export) and run it against the built artifact before shipping. Detector: TEST-NONE.

cross-cutting.title: node --check rejects non-.js extensions and a check on its own line does not gate the commit and deploy
cross-cutting.symptom: `node --check src/private/deck.js.txt` threw ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION, but because it sat on a separate line from the ship commands, the deploy shipped anyway with syntax never checked.
cross-cutting.fix: Copy to a temp .js and node --check that, and chain the whole ritual with && (or set -e) so a failing check stops commit and deploy.

cross-cutting.title: Permanently skipped tests present as dead coverage
cross-cutting.symptom: The suite reports passing while meaningful cases are disabled, overstating real coverage.
cross-cutting.fix: Fix it or delete it — a skipped test is not coverage. If it must stay, give it an owner and an expiry. Detector: TEST-SKIPPED.

cross-cutting.title: simctl defaults write seeds the wrong domain: the iOS app never sees the injected token while read-back 'works'
cross-cutting.symptom: A seeded auth token read back correctly but the native app always showed the login screen.
cross-cutting.fix: Resolve the container with simctl get_app_container booted <bundle> data, write the plist there, then relaunch so bootstrap() reads it. (A later hang was the disk-starved simulator, not the code.)

cross-cutting.title: Smoke tests ran against the wrong app because a 200 from localhost:<port> was another project's dev server
cross-cutting.symptom: The Pixelbake Teams UI walk printed a tick for every screen with page titles 'undefined' and a console error from '[abba]'; elsewhere preview_start refused ports 8791 (joy-cloud) and 8812 (postplan) held by other chats.
cross-cutting.fix: Moved the harness to a free port (5231) and asserted a page marker (title or handle) before trusting any screenshot; check lsof -iTCP:<port> or use autoPort before starting.

cross-cutting.title: Tests exist but no CI runs them
cross-cutting.symptom: A regression reaches production even though a test covering it exists, because nobody ran the suite.
cross-cutting.fix: Add a CI workflow that runs the suite on every push and blocks deploy on failure. Detector: TEST-NO-CI.

cross-cutting.title: compose.mjs headless-Chrome render has no timeout and a shared profile, so one wedged render stalls a whole creative run
cross-cutting.symptom: Renders stopped on the second image in two sessions (600s tool timeouts, runs pushed to the background, leftover chrome-apz-compose processes); a carousel export using --allow-file-access hung until a fresh profile was used.
cross-cutting.fix: Fresh mkdtemp user-data-dir per render, a hard timeout (perl alarm because macOS has no timeout command), up to four retries, the target PNG removed before each try, own stale chrome processes killed first. Nine slides then exported in a loop with per-slide exit status.

cross-cutting.title: Duplicate event listeners stack up on every re-render/re-mount
cross-cutting.symptom: A click/submit/keypress handler fires 2x, 3x, Nx (double submits, doubled network calls, runaway toasts); memory grows the longer the SPA session stays open and the tab gets sluggish.
cross-cutting.fix: Register global listeners once outside the render path, or in a mount hook with a symmetric removeEventListener cleanup; for dynamic lists use one delegated listener on a stable parent. Use a named function reference (not an inline arrow) so removal actually matches.

cross-cutting.title: Worker subrequest limit (50 free / 1000 paid per request) — serial fan-out stalls or throws Subrequest Limit Exceeded
cross-cutting.symptom: A Worker that fans out many fetch()/KV/R2 calls in one request either stalls (serial) or throws 'Subrequest Limit Exceeded'.
cross-cutting.fix: Batch/limit concurrency (Promise.all in capped chunks), cache, and keep per-request subrequests well under the plan limit.

cross-cutting.title: Worker subrequest limit hit by per-row D1/KV/fetch in a loop
cross-cutting.symptom: A request that iterates over a list and does a DB/KV/fetch call per item suddenly throws 'Too many subrequests' (or the CRON/batch job dies partway) once the list grows; fine with small demo data.
cross-cutting.fix: Collapse N calls into one: batch D1 with db.batch()/a single JOIN, use KV bulk/list, cache repeated fetches; move genuinely large fan-out to a Queue or Workflow. Catch the limit exception so the job resumes rather than silently truncating.

cross-cutting.title: No Open Graph or Twitter card — shared links render as a bare URL
cross-cutting.symptom: Pasting the product link into a message, Slack or social post shows a naked URL with no title, description or image, so nobody clicks.
cross-cutting.fix: Add og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630) and twitter:card to every shareable page, and verify with a card validator. Detector: SEO-NO-OG.

cross-cutting.title: No viewport meta — the page renders desktop-width on phones
cross-cutting.symptom: On a phone the whole layout is zoomed out and tiny, or controls run off the edge of the screen.
cross-cutting.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">. This is also the root cause behind many 'control is off-screen on mobile' reports. Detector: SEO-NO-VIEWPORT.

cross-cutting.title: Page has no <title> or meta description
cross-cutting.symptom: Browser tabs read 'index.html' or the domain, and search results show a machine-generated snippet.
cross-cutting.fix: Give every page a unique descriptive <title> and a meta description written for a human reading a search result. Detectors: SEO-NO-TITLE, SEO-NO-DESC.

cross-cutting.title: Later same-specificity CSS rule silently overrides mobile media query
cross-cutting.symptom: A mobile-only sizing rule had no effect; the element overflowed off-screen on phones.
cross-cutting.fix: Place responsive/mobile overrides after the global rules they must beat (or raise their specificity); verify computed width, not just that the rule exists.

cross-cutting.title: LLM replies shown in plain-text surfaces carry literal ** markers and ```json fences
cross-cutting.symptom: Hallalu recap emails opened with '**Here's a quick recap:**' under a second recap header; Abba's Ask Ava showed asterisks around bold words; /api/ai with a JSON-only prompt returned text starting with a ```json fence.
cross-cutting.fix: The recap prompt now demands plain text with no markdown and a single recap header; Abba added a small bold and italic renderer for Ava output; the client JSON extractor strips fences. The portal Ava draft path was not checked for fence handling.

cross-cutting.title: Background research agents were killed repeatedly by 'computer went to sleep mid-response' and whole runs were lost
cross-cutting.symptom: GMAT, GRE (twice), Phrases and a GRE top-up agents all failed with the same error; only one had saved partial output.
cross-cutting.fix: Run long agent batches under caffeinate -i, have agents append results to a file as they go (the GRE top-up kept 433 entries A-R that way), and resume from the partial file.

cross-cutting.title: Browser-pane javascript_tool shares one global scope: re-declaring const across calls and top-level await both throw
cross-cutting.symptom: Consecutive calls failed with 'Identifier c has already been declared' and 'await is only valid in async functions', wasting verification round-trips.
cross-cutting.fix: Wrap every snippet in an IIFE, (async()=>{...})() when awaiting, and return JSON.stringify of the result.

cross-cutting.title: Commands handed to the user's zsh failed twice: a [!.] glob hit history expansion and BSD du refused -s with -d while stderr went to /dev/null
cross-cutting.symptom: The pasted 'sudo du -shx /Users/rhemajoy/* /Users/rhemajoy/.[!.]*' returned 'zsh: event not found: .]'; the replacement 'sudo du -shx -d1' returned nothing because BSD du rejects -s combined with -d and the error was discarded, costing three more round trips
cross-cutting.fix: For user-run commands avoid ! in globs, use find -maxdepth 1 or du -hx -d1 without -s, keep stderr, and write output to a file the agent reads rather than asking for a paste

cross-cutting.title: Concurrent session commit swept another session's staged files (shared git index)
cross-cutting.symptom: A commit contained unrelated files staged by a parallel Claude session.
cross-cutting.fix: Stage explicit paths and use git apply --cached for hunks, check git status before commit, and prefer a worktree per session.

cross-cutting.title: du run as the user reported ~/Pictures as 416 KB when it held 57 GB, so the home folder was measured at 36 GB instead of 89 GB
cross-cutting.symptom: A disk-full cleanup chased a phantom 115-160 GB of 'root-owned' data through four wrong sudo commands before sudo du showed Photo Booth Library 36 GB and Photos Library 20 GB; /System showed 184 GB because the Data volume is firmlinked under it
cross-cutting.fix: Run sudo du -hx -d2 on the home folder first, never trust a non-sudo total that does not reconcile with df, keep stderr visible, and ignore /System when summing the Data volume

cross-cutting.title: Full-disk state is misdiagnosed: sealed-snapshot df, unwritable tool output and a blocking shell update prompt
cross-cutting.symptom: Bash commands looked failed with no output; df showed 12Gi used and 0 free on a 228Gi disk; a terminal tab sat on an oh-my-zsh 'Would you like to update? [Y/n]' prompt; a read-only df was denied by the classifier as a false positive.
cross-cutting.fix: Check /System/Volumes/Data (5.7 GiB free while the snapshot showed 630 MiB), free regenerable caches first (npm, wrangler, pip), set DISABLE_UPDATE_PROMPT=true for agent terminals, and retry a denied read-only command with a different tool.

cross-cutting.title: gh repo create --source=. ran from the wrong directory because the shell cwd resets between commands
cross-cutting.symptom: A new GitHub repository was wired to the pitch folder instead of the project.
cross-cutting.fix: Always cd inside the same command (cd project && gh repo create ...) or pass an absolute path, then verify git remote -v.

cross-cutting.title: git filter-branch run from a repo subdirectory silently did nothing because stderr was discarded; 12 trailers survived in one repo
cross-cutting.symptom: A four-repo loop rewrote three repos but PlannerStudio/webapp still showed 12 Co-Authored-By trailers on main; the loop printed no error.
cross-cutting.fix: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" before filter-branch; verify with `git log main --grep` (not --all, which also counts refs/original backups) and never blanket-discard stderr on destructive history operations.

cross-cutting.title: git push --force-with-lease rejected with 'stale info' after filter-branch -- --all, reflog expire and gc
cross-cutting.symptom: All four rewritten repos failed to push main with '[rejected] main -> main (stale info)'.
cross-cutting.fix: For these solo, user-authorised repos used plain git push --force and verified origin/main (0 trailers, same commit counts); in shared repos capture the old SHA first and use --force-with-lease=main:<old-sha>.

cross-cutting.title: GNU timeout does not exist on macOS, so a guarded find scan returned nothing and read as 'no results'
cross-cutting.symptom: `timeout 120 find ...` with stderr discarded printed no output; a reconciliation concluded there were no files until `which timeout gtimeout` showed neither exists.
cross-cutting.fix: Do not wrap commands in timeout on macOS (use perl -e alarm, or background+kill, or run plain); never discard stderr on discovery scans.

cross-cutting.title: The definition-of-done skill committed and deployed but never pushed: eight commits sat unpushed until the user asked
cross-cutting.symptom: On Hallalu a finish pass found eight unpushed commits on main (v264 to v271) after the work had been reported as finished; the user separately asked that /finish also push.
cross-cutting.fix: The /finish description and checklist now say pushed to git; if there is no remote, say so and skip rather than leave a pushable commit behind. Evertrue was given a private GitHub remote.

cross-cutting.title: Two sessions deploying one Worker from the same working tree shipped each other's half-finished edits
cross-cutting.symptom: A live deploy contained another session's uncommitted changes and broke a route.
cross-cutting.fix: Deploy only from a clean, committed tree (or an isolated worktree with symlinked node_modules) and verify the pushed commit builds there first.

cross-cutting.title: Unquoted URL containing ? aborts in zsh with no matches found and an empty fetch looks like a hash mismatch
cross-cutting.symptom: curl on an unquoted URL printed zsh: no matches found, the empty body hashed to e3b0c442..., which was misread as a changed page.
cross-cutting.fix: Always single-quote URLs, and treat e3b0c44298fc1c14... as the signal that the fetch returned nothing.

cross-cutting.title: Unquoted zsh grep --include glob returns false negatives (searched nothing, concluded absence)
cross-cutting.symptom: A search that should hit returned empty, leading an agent to declare a feature missing.
cross-cutting.fix: Always quote globs, prefer rg, sanity-check the search with a known positive, and never remove capability on a negative finding.

cross-cutting.title: UTF-8 static HTML without a <meta charset> showed mojibake when served by python http.server (no charset header)
cross-cutting.symptom: em dashes, middle dots and arrows rendered as garbled Latin-1 sequences in the preview
cross-cutting.fix: added <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first element of the head

cross-cutting.title: Verification navigated the owner's pinned live-board tab away and the board log was lost from view
cross-cutting.symptom: The owner had asked for the Aprizely live board to stay open; a demo check was loaded into that same Browser-pane tab and the owner complained.
cross-cutting.fix: Open a dedicated verification tab (tabs_create, not foreground) and never navigate a tab the owner asked to keep open; restore the board URL if it was changed.

cross-cutting.title: wrangler d1 create failed at the account's database-count cap while a rename plan assumed an unlimited number of databases
cross-cutting.symptom: Renaming CocoMail to Joy needed a new D1 database and the create call answered 'On the Workers Free plan? Upgrade to create more'; the session had to delete its own empty database and recreate it, and had already created the new R2 bucket and worker
cross-cutting.fix: Check wrangler d1 list against the cap before any rename, create the replacement first only when there is room, and prefer reusing a database or prefixing tables over adding one per tiny app

cross-cutting.title: wrangler d1 migrations apply replays old migrations when earlier ones were applied with d1 execute (empty d1_migrations table)
cross-cutting.symptom: Applying migration 007 failed because 006 re-ran and its column already existed; the tracking table was empty.
cross-cutting.fix: Backfilled d1_migrations rows for 001-006, then applied 007; pick one mechanism per database from day one.

cross-cutting.title: wrangler email sending returns Unauthorized 2036 on every call even after a fresh login adds the email_sending scope, until the product is activated in the dashboard
cross-cutting.symptom: Both 'enable' and a plain 'list' failed with code 2036 after wrangler whoami listed email_sending (write); only a one-time dashboard activation (Email, Email Sending, Get started) followed by wrangler email sending enable worked
cross-cutting.fix: On 2036 with the scope present, send the user to the dashboard activation first; then enable the zone, check DKIM, SPF and DMARC records, and add the send_email binding

cross-cutting.title: wrangler r2 object get writes a 0-byte file because it defaults to local simulated storage unless --remote is passed
cross-cutting.symptom: Pulling a stored .eml to check its Authentication-Results header produced an empty file and no error, so the first check appeared to find no headers
cross-cutting.fix: Pass --remote when reading production objects and test the byte count before parsing

cross-cutting.title: zsh does not word-split an unquoted $VAR in a for loop: the repo loop ran once with the whole string, so cd failed and nothing was pushed
cross-cutting.symptom: for r in $REPOS; do cd $HOME/$r ... done printed CD_FAIL after one iteration under the Bash tool's zsh
cross-cutting.fix: moved the loop into a bash script file and re-ran; use arrays or run multi-repo loops under bash

cross-cutting.title: zsh loop variable named path clobbers PATH so every later command is not found
cross-cutting.symptom: After a for path in ... loop in zsh, tail, python3 and other tools failed with command not found for the rest of that shell session.
cross-cutting.fix: Never use path (or the other tied names cdpath, fpath, manpath) as a loop or scratch variable in zsh; use p or file_path.

cross-cutting.title: zsh unquoted --include=*.js aborts grep with 'no matches found' and reads as 'not found'
cross-cutting.symptom: Searches like `grep -rniE 'x' --include=*.js .` printed '(eval):N: no matches found: --include=*.js', leading the agent to conclude strings did not exist when they did.
cross-cutting.fix: Quote globs (--include='*.js'), prefer rg or a node one-liner, and treat empty grep output as 'search failed' until stderr is checked.

cross-cutting.title: zsh: using `path` as a read/loop variable overwrites $PATH, so every later command is 'command not found: git/curl'
cross-cutting.symptom: A verification loop (`while IFS=$'\t' read -r slug path; do git show HEAD:worker.js ...`) printed 'command not found: git' on every iteration and reported all 34 images 'missing'; a second session's `path=${pair#*:}` loop then broke curl the same way. The misleading output was first dismissed as a 'PATH quirk'.
cross-cutting.fix: Rename the variable (pth, rel, p2). When 'command not found' appears for a command that worked seconds earlier, echo $PATH before debugging anything else. Hit in two separate sessions on 2026-09-08 and 2026-10-01.

Aprizely.title: Account switcher returns the raw session token in login JSON and stores it in localStorage for 60 days (also in Breadcrumb)
Aprizely.symptom: A single XSS can read every remembered account's session token and take over those accounts.
Aprizely.fix: Keep switch tokens server-side keyed by an opaque device id in an HttpOnly cookie, or store them encrypted with a per-device key and require a PIN to switch.

Aprizely.title: javascript:/data: URL scheme click-XSS via stored and AI-sourced links
Aprizely.symptom: A live_url/repo_url/pitch_url — or an AI-sourced competitor URL — set to javascript:… became a clickable href that ran script on click
Aprizely.fix: Added a safeUrl() guard (http/https only, else '#') applied across all 9 href sites, including AI competitor links

Aprizely.title: Public handle-availability endpoint lets anyone enumerate existing account handles
Aprizely.symptom: An unauthenticated signup helper reports whether a handle is taken, and a code comment accepts that handles are semi-public. Any script can probe candidate handles and learn which accounts exist, including the owner's account.
Aprizely.fix: Keep the check but give it a low per-IP budget, check availability only at submit time where possible, and rely on the existing lockout so a known handle is not a cheap first step; consider a generic response for taken handles on the login screen.

Aprizely.title: Temporary account passcode echoed into chat and tool output and passed on the command line
Aprizely.symptom: While seeding the owner's account, the generated 6-digit temporary passcode was printed by cat of seed/.passcode.txt, passed as a process argument to seed.mjs, and repeated in the final chat message, so it now sits in the session transcript.
Aprizely.fix: Generate the passcode, write it to a mode-600 file and print only the path; pass it by environment variable or stdin instead of argv; force a change on first login; never quote it in the reply.

Aprizely.title: Inherited 20,000-character clamp on note text would silently cut a long dictation
Aprizely.symptom: A dictation longer than about 25 minutes of speech would be truncated on save while the UI promised the exact transcript was kept; the voice-note recorder also stopped at 5 minutes.
Aprizely.fix: Raise note text to 200,000 characters, the summariser input to 100,000 and the recording cap to 60 minutes (done).

Aprizely.title: Demo mode threw 'Cannot access id before initialization' when logging a cost or payment
Aprizely.symptom: In ?demo, POST /costs and POST /payments raised a ReferenceError.
Aprizely.fix: Hoist const id to the top of the DEMO block. Found by exercising the new payment sort in demo.

Aprizely.title: One malformed report blanked the entire Reports list
Aprizely.symptom: The whole Reports view rendered blank when a single report had a string (not array) tasks field
Aprizely.fix: Make reportCard defensive so a malformed report degrades gracefully and never breaks the list

Aprizely.title: A 22-app, 285-log bulk sync landed on the wrong account because the saved agent token belonged to the seed user
Aprizely.symptom: The portfolio sync and report appeared under @rhema while the user was looking at @rhe.
Aprizely.fix: Run whoami and compare with the expected handle before any bulk write; show the handle in the CLI output of start and finish.

Aprizely.title: Agent token and board state shared one file (~/.aprizely.json): state writes clobbered the token
Aprizely.symptom: apz.mjs reported 'no token' after a board start/step because state overwrote the saved token.
Aprizely.fix: Keep token and state in separate files, merge on write, and never replace the credential file from the state path.

Aprizely.title: /app HTML shell edge-cached with no Cache-Control, so the plain URL kept pointing at the old /_v path after deploy
Aprizely.symptom: After deploying ASSET_VER r53, plain /app still referenced /_v/r52/app.js while /app?cb=... returned r53.
Aprizely.fix: Verify with a cache-busted fetch. The durable fix is Cache-Control: no-store on the rewritten HTML (as done on Evertrue).

Aprizely.title: app.js changes shipped without bumping ASSET_VER, so cached browsers kept the old build
Aprizely.symptom: The new KPI tile was missing in the pane after deploy, and the previous task's 'Work & reports' panel had never reached cached browsers either.
Aprizely.fix: Bumped ASSET_VER to r53 and corrected the memory note. The constant could instead be derived from a content hash at deploy.

Aprizely.title: Worklog state keyed by cwd is shared by concurrent sessions run from the same directory
Aprizely.symptom: From ~, apz done N returned 'done <index> out of range' and the board tab showed 0/13. The shared ~/.aprizely.worklog.json held another session's Capital Signal board, so this session's ticks were applied to, or rejected by, the wrong board.
Aprizely.fix: Workaround used: cd into a dedicated project dir and rebuild the state file. Proper fix: key state by session id (APZ_SESSION env or --id) or refuse start when an unfinished board exists in that cwd.

Aprizely.title: A payment added today did not appear at the top of the ledger and the root cause was never found
Aprizely.symptom: Owner logged a payment and could not find it in the list.
Aprizely.fix: Render sorts a copy of S.payments by at descending before slice(0, 12), the payment sheet has a date field (default today, timezone-corrected) and shows a 'today' badge. Reproduce with real data to confirm.

Aprizely.title: Account totals computed client-side from a capped page of rows undercount
Aprizely.symptom: Any sum of runs or reports in the browser could only reflect the 20 worklogs and 60 reports that /api/state returned, against 205 and 191 stored.
Aprizely.fix: Added a server-side lifetime aggregate (runs, reports, work_ms) to /api/state as S.totals, with a client fallback for demo mode. Also raised the worklogs limit from 20 to 100 so project runs load.

Aprizely.title: Account work total inflated to 1148h by boards left 'active'
Aprizely.symptom: The first server aggregate of work logged read 1148h across 208 runs.
Aprizely.fix: Cap each run at 4h in both the SQL aggregate and agentSessionDur, giving 233h47m. A run's duration should come from finished where present.

Aprizely.title: Agent API matches project names exactly, so Bug Ledger created a duplicate of the seeded BugLedger card with no way to merge
Aprizely.symptom: A second Bug Ledger card appeared next to BugLedger and the agent API has no rename or delete.
Aprizely.fix: Normalise names (strip spaces and punctuation) or accept an alias list in project resolution, and add an owner-only merge in the app.

Aprizely.title: apz start --tasks silently splits notes on ';' and '|', creating stray tasks that shift every index
Aprizely.symptom: A note such as 'Diagnose::...(HTTP 200); returning-user boot awaits /me...' became its own task. Boards came out with 7 tasks instead of 6, 8 instead of 7 and 16 instead of 6, so done <index> ticked the wrong task or went out of range.
Aprizely.fix: Workaround: avoid ';' and '|' in notes and inspect .aprizely.worklog.json indices after start. Proper fix: only split on '|' outside a note, support an escape, and print the parsed task list on start.

Aprizely.title: apz step used as a read probe re-opened a finished task, and done indices ignore #Wave headers
Aprizely.symptom: Running step 0 to dump state dropped progress from 15/23 to 14/23, and done 2 ticked a different task than expected.
Aprizely.fix: Add apz tasks (read-only, prints index and status), make step on a done task a no-op, and document that indices exclude headers.

Aprizely.title: Board time was misleading: flat 15m/task estimate beside seconds of real work, and an idle active wave kept its real clock ticking (22m for a 5s step)
Aprizely.symptom: A 5-second wave read '~30m' and the header claimed '~1h est' for seconds of work; a demo board left with an active wave showed 22m 14s of 'real' time long after nothing was happening.
Aprizely.fix: Adaptive ETA from the mean duration of completed tasks (in-progress task counts down), falling back to a (~Nm) token then the default; real clock freezes when the board has been idle more than 3 minutes since the last update; done waves show actual only, active shows actual + ~left, pending shows ~estimate. Verified live on the stale board (22m collapsed to 2s).

Aprizely.title: Break-even card said 'covers 100%' when revenue was 152% of costs
Aprizely.symptom: Finance dashboard displayed 'covers 100%' even though MRR was 152% of monthly costs
Aprizely.fix: Compute and show the true coverage ratio (e.g. 152%) rather than a hardcoded/clamped 100%

Aprizely.title: Costs could not carry a renewal anchor: costCols never read b.started and createCost always stamped now()
Aprizely.symptom: No way to say when a subscription first charged, so next-charge dates could not be computed or shown; Costs and Stack were one table mixing paid and free tools.
Aprizely.fix: costCols reads started, createCost uses c.started || now(), PATCH accepts it; nextCharge/renewLabel roll the date forward by cycle (shown as 'Sep 2 in 7d', due ones highlighted); a 'first charged' field stores noon to dodge timezone day shift; Costs tab shows paid items only and Stack lists all tools with a 'free' chip.

Aprizely.title: DELETE /api/account confirmation body was never read because the worker parsed JSON only for POST and PATCH
Aprizely.symptom: The client sends the delete-account confirmation in the body of a DELETE request, but the worker ignored it, so the confirm check could not work as designed.
Aprizely.fix: Parse the JSON body for DELETE as well, inside the same size-capped block (done), or move the confirmation into the URL. Add a test that every destructive route rejects a missing confirm value.

Aprizely.title: Live board showed no per-wave time on any board without (~Nm) tokens because tasks carried no start/done timestamps
Aprizely.symptom: After a per-wave/total ETA feature shipped, normal boards (no (~25m) token in labels) still showed no per-wave time, which looked like 'the old version is still running' even though the feature was committed and deployed.
Aprizely.fix: Server now stamps startedAt/doneAt onto each task inside the existing tasks JSON as statuses change (merged by index from the previous row, no D1 migration); the board derives per-wave real elapsed; /api/agent/report pulls the same stamped timestamps so the published report groups the timeline by wave with real times. Proven live on a token-less board.

Aprizely.title: Live-board ETA rollup undercounted when a wave mixed a wave-level token with a few task tokens
Aprizely.symptom: The header would have shown ~8m total instead of ~60m on the board that carried both kinds of token.
Aprizely.fix: Wave token wins when present (waveEta||taskEta) and the total is the sum of per-wave values; per-task badges still show on each row.

Aprizely.title: Per-project and weekly time ignored agent run durations
Aprizely.symptom: The Work Log 'This week' bars and the per-project totals were empty even with 205 logged agent runs.
Aprizely.fix: Added agentSessionDur(worklog) to both functions and a 'Work & reports' panel (time, runs, reports with links) to the project modal.

Aprizely.title: Report ship card says 'Deployed: Not deployed yet' for Cloudflare deploys
Aprizely.symptom: A report published after a verified wrangler deploy still showed 'Not deployed yet'.
Aprizely.fix: Open. Either pass the deploy flag explicitly, or have apz read the last wrangler version/timestamp when building the ship card.

Aprizely.title: Work Log tab was empty despite weeks of agent work: it only showed personal timers while agent boards live in a separate store
Aprizely.symptom: The owner saw nothing in Work Log although boards and reports existed.
Aprizely.fix: Work Log now lists every agent session itemised by wave (each task with its description), linked to its project, timestamped with duration and live/report links, plus a per-day work-time analysis that merges timers, agent sessions and payments, with the week graph at the top.

Aprizely.title: worker.js is classed as binary data, so plain grep silently returned zero matches
Aprizely.symptom: grep for 'worklog' and 'live' in the 77KB, 1314-line src/worker.js returned nothing, while the file clearly serves /live.
Aprizely.fix: Use grep -a. Find and remove the stray control bytes so the source is text again.

Aprizely.title: Activity timeline dumped the entire status_note field
Aprizely.symptom: status_note edits printed the whole note into the activity timeline, cluttering it
Aprizely.fix: Truncate long field values in the activity event builder so entries stay tidy

Aprizely.title: Bulk rename introduced a grammar slip ('a account')
Aprizely.symptom: A bulk find-replace of 'studio' → 'account' produced 'a account' where the article should agree ('an account').
Aprizely.fix: Corrected 'a account' → 'an account' and verified the copy renders live; left the internal importStudio() function name (never user-visible) untouched. Lesson: after a bulk rename, grep for 'a <newword>' article mismatches.

Aprizely.title: Negative currency rendered as $-59.17 instead of minus-$59.17
Aprizely.symptom: Negative money values showed the minus sign after the dollar sign
Aprizely.fix: Format negatives with the minus before the currency symbol in the shared money formatter

Aprizely.title: New spend markers rendered '$ GBP23' because money() takes a currency symbol and the code passed a nonexistent S.user.currency defaulting to 'GBP'
Aprizely.symptom: Demo render of the new work-time analysis showed a doubled symbol and ISO code.
Aprizely.fix: Use S.user.baseCurrency || '$' and drop the icon. Caught only because the demo render was inspected.

Aprizely.title: New token button did nothing when the browser suppressed window.prompt()
Aprizely.symptom: Clicking New token in Settings produced no prompt and no error in embedded browsers.
Aprizely.fix: Replace prompt() with an inline form (done) and never branch on prompt() alone.

Aprizely.title: Unlock keypad numbers float high and misalign
Aprizely.symptom: On the unlock PIN pad the numbers sat too high inside their circles and 1/0 didn't line up with the lettered keys — it still looked off after a first tidy pass.
Aprizely.fix: Centered each number dead-centre in the key and absolute-positioned the letters tucked at the bottom; added a hairline border + subtle fill, tighter spacing and a smoother press state; also relabeled 'Create a studio' → 'Create account' on the unlock screen.

Aprizely.title: Control-character regex was saved with literal control bytes, which broke edits and risks bundler and git trouble
Aprizely.symptom: The clean() sanitiser line in worker.js showed as a mangled character class under cat -v (raw NUL, BS and VT bytes inside the regex), and an Edit whose old_string was copied from it failed with string not found.
Aprizely.fix: Rewrote the line with escaped forms (u0000-u0008, u000b, u000c, u000e-u001f written as escape sequences) using a small script and verified with grep -c u0000. Add a pre-commit or deploy check that fails on any control byte other than tab, LF and CR in source files.

Aprizely.title: npx --no-install wrangler deploy fails for a project pinning a wrangler version that is not installed locally, and a grep-filtered deploy hid the failure
Aprizely.symptom: Aprizely's SEO tag deploy printed nothing useful under grep -iE 'Uploaded|Deployed|Version ID'; re-running showed 'npx canceled due to missing packages and no YES option: wrangler@4.145.0'.
Aprizely.fix: Use npx --yes wrangler deploy (or install the pinned version) and include 'error|✘' in the grep; confirm a Current Version ID line before saying deployed.

Aprizely.title: schema.sql no longer matches the live D1 database (columns and tables added by hand)
Aprizely.symptom: The repo schema.sql lacks columns that production relies on (base_currency and categories on users; pitch_url, category and active_users on projects) and has no CREATE TABLE for reports at all, yet the README tells you to run schema.sql once to bootstrap. A fresh deploy or a restore from the repo cannot reproduce production.
Aprizely.fix: Reconcile schema.sql with sqlite_master from the live database now; from then on write every change as a numbered migrations/NNN.sql applied with d1 execute --file, and add a schema:check script that diffs PRAGMA table_info against schema.sql and runs before deploy.

Aprizely.title: Worker serving index.html through the ASSETS binding looped on 307 redirects, and the 307 stayed edge-cached
Aprizely.symptom: Right after the first deploy, / and /app returned an empty 307 instead of the page. /index.html redirected to /, the Worker handles / first (run_worker_first) and fetches /index.html again, so the pretty-URL redirect bounced. After html_handling was set to none, plain /app kept returning the cached 307 for a while while the same URL with a cache-busting query string already returned 200.
Aprizely.fix: Set assets.html_handling to none in wrangler.json whenever the Worker serves HTML from ASSETS for run_worker_first paths, and fetch the explicit .html asset path. After deploying, check the plain URL with curl -sI and again with a cache-busting query string; if only the plain URL still shows a 307, wait or purge rather than redeploying.

Stitchhooky.title: Co-stitch rooms and theme leak across accounts
Stitchhooky.symptom: The next person on the device auto-joined your live co-stitch room and kept your theme.
Stitchhooky.fix: Scoped co-stitch rooms and appearance per account so they no longer leak between users.

Stitchhooky.title: Security headers silently ignored
Stitchhooky.symptom: Security/CSP headers added in the worker did nothing.
Stitchhooky.fix: Moved the headers to the proper `_headers` mechanism.

Stitchhooky.title: Stored-XSS vectors in user content
Stitchhooky.symptom: Multiple stored-XSS injection points, including an unescaped server value reaching an HTML attribute.
Stitchhooky.fix: Escaped the values and closed all five stored-XSS vectors.

Stitchhooky.title: 'Reset everything' resurrects data on reload
Stitchhooky.symptom: Resetting everything did not stick; data came back on the next reload.
Stitchhooky.fix: Made reset also clear the rolling backup so it no longer resurrects.

Stitchhooky.title: Cross-account data leak on shared device
Stitchhooky.symptom: A second person signing up on the same device saw the first user's projects and streak.
Stitchhooky.fix: Scoped storage per account so a new user starts empty (proven: Bea sees zero projects).

Stitchhooky.title: Duplicate chart projects on every reload
Stitchhooky.symptom: Reloading created a brand-new duplicate of the same chart project (three identically-named ones appeared).
Stitchhooky.fix: Persisted savedId so a chart maps to one project.

Stitchhooky.title: Projects view wiped by a single corrupt save
Stitchhooky.symptom: The projects view went blank with no warning.
Stitchhooky.fix: Added backups and recovery (preserve the broken copy) and made each card render independently so one bad project can't blank the list.

Stitchhooky.title: Resize wipes the canvas artwork
Stitchhooky.symptom: Resizing the grid erased the user's drawing.
Stitchhooky.fix: Resize now preserves existing artwork.

Stitchhooky.title: Sign-up orphans or clobbers pre-account data
Stitchhooky.symptom: Signing up could vanish pre-account projects or clobber an existing local store for a handle.
Stitchhooky.fix: Pre-account projects are adopted by the first signer, and sign-up refuses a handle with an existing store and points to sign-in.

Stitchhooky.title: Boot crash from temporal dead zone
Stitchhooky.symptom: The entire app died on first load with no console error.
Stitchhooky.fix: Reordered initialization so `db` exists before it is referenced.

Stitchhooky.title: HUD crash on second render
Stitchhooky.symptom: Every count after the first would crash.
Stitchhooky.fix: Reworked renderCover to not reference the destroyed element.

Stitchhooky.title: LS_BAK temporal dead zone crash
Stitchhooky.symptom: The app refused to boot.
Stitchhooky.fix: Moved the declaration before it is used.

Stitchhooky.title: Passcode lockout with no escape hatch
Stitchhooky.symptom: User was asked for a passcode they never set and could not get in.
Stitchhooky.fix: Added a forgot-passcode escape hatch (fixed three ways) and cleared the stray flag.

Stitchhooky.title: Cell-click runs past end of row
Stitchhooky.symptom: Clicking a cell could advance past the last stitch of a row into the next one.
Stitchhooky.fix: Clamped cell clicks to the current row's end.

Stitchhooky.title: Chart collapses to a tiny thumbnail
Stitchhooky.symptom: The chart shrank to a thumbnail inside a huge empty page card.
Stitchhooky.fix: Removed transform-scaling and made the grid fill the page width with real cells.

Stitchhooky.title: Chart-grow message flow miscounts
Stitchhooky.symptom: The chart stage didn't repaint per message, the prompt offered to add skips instead of stitches, and it grew the wrong row.
Stitchhooky.fix: Repaint per message, name real stitches, and grow the correct row (verified 30→32).

Stitchhooky.title: Community tab is a dead end
Stitchhooky.symptom: Community refused with a toast telling the user to sign in via Settings.
Stitchhooky.fix: Fixed the Community entry so it no longer dead-ends.

Stitchhooky.title: Competing writers miscount home tiles
Stitchhooky.symptom: The home tile still counted 13 stitches from a stale value.
Stitchhooky.fix: Consolidated to a single ppMeta writer.

Stitchhooky.title: Dictation mic leak into counting view
Stitchhooky.symptom: After dictating rows then hitting Save & start counting, speech kept appending rows to a stale draft instead of counting.
Stitchhooky.fix: Mic now hard-stops on entering the counting studio.

Stitchhooky.title: Learn-to-read-charts modal silently fails
Stitchhooky.symptom: Opening 'Learn to read charts' did nothing visible.
Stitchhooky.fix: Fixed the modal so the guide opens correctly.

Stitchhooky.title: Magic-ring foundation stitches collapsed to one cell
Stitchhooky.symptom: Round 1 of nearly every amigurumi ('6 sc in magic ring') counted as a single stitch, undercounting the row.
Stitchhooky.fix: Distinguished ring/foundation targets (expand to N individual cells) from a cluster worked into a single stitch (stays grouped).

Stitchhooky.title: New project would not save and gave no reason: the validation error only appeared on the Type tab and typed-but-unadded row text was discarded
Stitchhooky.symptom: The owner reported new projects not saving; Save did nothing visible, especially when the user was on another editor tab or had typed a row without pressing Add.
Stitchhooky.fix: Show a visible error beside the Save button, auto-switch to the Type tab and scroll the input into view, and commitPendingRows() so uncommitted input is added before validation.

Stitchhooky.title: Notation parser undercounts stitches ('7 vs 18')
Stitchhooky.symptom: Stitch totals came out far too low, e.g. reporting 7 when it should be 18.
Stitchhooky.fix: Parser overhaul plus a `normalizeNotation` that folds standing/stacked/foundation/post/Ntog/magic-ring variants into keys.

Stitchhooky.title: Marketing says 'no account, no ads' but the backend has accounts, social and Stripe subscriptions
Stitchhooky.symptom: The product markets itself as 'no account, no ads', while the backend has full email/password + TOTP accounts, social follows/posts/photos and live Stripe subscriptions ($4/mo, $24/yr).
Stitchhooky.fix: Open: rewrite the claim to match the real data flows and align the privacy policy, or gate accounts as optional. Needs a copy fix plus a source-verified claim review.

Stitchhooky.title: Shipped with ~30 high-severity accessibility gaps across the web surface
Stitchhooky.symptom: Scanner flagged ~30 HIGH accessibility issues: icon-only controls with no accessible name, images with no alt, inputs with no label.
Stitchhooky.fix: aria-label every icon button, alt every content image, label every input, set <html lang>; re-run A11Y-* detectors before ship and mirror the fixes to the native surfaces to keep parity.

Stitchhooky.title: Billing panel invisible at 0x0
Stitchhooky.symptom: The billing panel had content but measured 0x0 and never showed.
Stitchhooky.fix: One layout rule fixed all eleven; billing now renders at 560x740.

Stitchhooky.title: Dead hero photo on landing page
Stitchhooky.symptom: The landing hero image 404'd, showing a broken tile.
Stitchhooky.fix: Swapped to a verified-200 photo and added a fallback that hides any tile whose image fails.

Stitchhooky.title: Duplicate DOM ids after bento redesign
Stitchhooky.symptom: Nine duplicate DOM ids made home-tile buttons behave unpredictably.
Stitchhooky.fix: Removed the leftover old tile row.

Stitchhooky.title: iOS text too close to phone edge
Stitchhooky.symptom: In the iOS simulator, words sat too close to the edge of the phone.
Stitchhooky.fix: Raised horizontal padding to 22pt with the title at 27pt.

Stitchhooky.title: Menu hidden behind next card
Stitchhooky.symptom: The project menu rendered behind the following card instead of on top.
Stitchhooky.fix: Fixed the stacking so the menu layers above adjacent cards.

Stitchhooky.title: Mic control runs off screen on real devices
Stitchhooky.symptom: The mic control ran off the edge of the screen on real devices.
Stitchhooky.fix: Corrected the viewport meta tag.

Stitchhooky.title: Mislabeled +n count bubble
Stitchhooky.symptom: The +n increment bubble showed the wrong number.
Stitchhooky.fix: Corrected the bubble's label calculation.

Stitchhooky.title: Pattern grid cells shrank to a 36px max width with flex:1 and were too small to tap, and count-screen bubbles covered the chart with no way to delete or edit them
Stitchhooky.symptom: Cells in long rows became tiny and hard to hit; on mobile the transcript bubbles and the dock's opaque gradient covered the chart behind them, and a mis-heard message could not be removed.
Stitchhooky.fix: Larger tappable cells that wrap (rather than shrink) with per-cell stitch labels and a settings toggle, delete/edit controls on each bubble, a lighter dock gradient and a shorter feed on mobile.

Stitchhooky.title: Settings button opened nothing
Stitchhooky.symptom: The Settings control was genuinely broken and didn't open the panel.
Stitchhooky.fix: Corrected the settings sheet structure so the panel opens.

Stitchhooky.title: Stale CSS rule squishes knit cells
Stitchhooky.symptom: Knit grid cells rendered square despite correct code.
Stitchhooky.fix: Removed the stale rule so per-craft geometry applies.

Stitchhooky.title: Tile colour clashes with theme accent
Stitchhooky.symptom: Tile colours (e.g. purple) did not match the theme the user picked.
Stitchhooky.fix: Tiles now follow the theme's colour and each tile background is picker-controlled.

Stitchhooky.title: CSP blocks YouTube thumbnails and embeds
Stitchhooky.symptom: The new CSP would have broken YouTube thumbnails and video embeds.
Stitchhooky.fix: Widened the CSP and re-verified zero blocked resources.

Stitchhooky.title: Users served stale app version
Stitchhooky.symptom: Returning users silently ran old JavaScript/HTML, making just-added features look missing.
Stitchhooky.fix: Bumped/regenerated the `?v=` stamps and made HTML always revalidate.

Abba.title: Private lesson and trade screenshots are served unauthenticated at /api/media/<key>, secrecy rests only on an unguessable key (low severity)
Abba.symptom: curl without an Authorization header returned 200 image/png for a lesson screenshot at /api/media/m/<32 hex>.png, the same as with a token.
Abba.fix: Not changed (design trade-off, keys are 128-bit random). Hardening options: short-lived signed URLs or an auth-cookie check for private kinds, plus deleting the R2 object when the lesson or trade is deleted.

Abba.title: PUT /api/trades/:id rewrites every column, so a client sending a partial trade silently nulls the rest
Abba.symptom: While adding trade editing to the native iPhone/Mac apps, the Swift Trade model lacked media/best/worst/confidence columns; saving an edit from it would have wiped those fields in D1.
Abba.fix: Extended the native Trade struct to carry every column and built a lossless Store.tradeBody for edits; the new strategies and notes.lesson PUTs were made merge-safe (partial PUT keeps all other fields, proven by curl). Rule recorded: never send a partial trade.

Abba.title: mxPop ReferenceError after a scripted patch silently no-oped
Abba.symptom: A feature wired through a scripted String.replace patch threw 'mxPop is not defined' at runtime; the patch printed success.
Abba.fix: Scripted patches must assert the anchor exists (throw if src.includes(anchor) is false) and assert the output differs; prefer the Edit tool or a quoted heredoc ('EOF') for code containing $ ( \ characters.

Abba.title: Native app aborted right after granting speech/microphone permission (AudioUnit RPC timeout)
Abba.symptom: Tapping Allow on the mic/speech prompt in the iOS simulator killed the app.
Abba.fix: Speech.swift gained an inputUnavailable state and a guard around starting the recogniser/audio engine so unavailable input is reported in the UI instead of aborting the process; rebuilt for iOS and Mac.

Abba.title: StudioTTS.stop was undefined: voice 'stop' wiring threw on tts.speak/stop alias mismatch
Abba.symptom: Pressing stop on spoken lessons threw TypeError (StudioTTS.stop is not a function) and audio kept playing.
Abba.fix: Add stop as an alias of cancel in the module and guard callers with typeof checks; add a smoke test that every public method name used by callers exists on the module object.

Abba.title: Native trades PUT replaces the whole record: partial updates from iPhone/Mac dropped fields (not merge-safe)
Abba.symptom: Editing one field in the native app could blank other trade fields saved by the web app.
Abba.fix: Send the complete freshly-fetched object, or add a server-side merge/PATCH; verify round-trip of every field in a cross-client test.

Abba.title: Calendar and day views grouped trades by the UTC date of an ISO timestamp, putting evening futures trades on the wrong day
Abba.symptom: Futures trades taken late in the local day appeared under the following calendar day, so per-day totals and per-trade minis in the month calendar were wrong.
Abba.fix: Day grouping now uses the trader's local date; verified both test futures trades group on the 24th with a +$1,600 total and per-trade minis.

Abba.title: Candle route regex rejected ETF/dotted/dashed tickers (400 on valid symbols)
Abba.symptom: Charts and bots returned 400 'bad symbol' for tickers such as BRK-B style or ETF symbols with punctuation.
Abba.fix: Widen to a bounded allowlist class (letters, digits, . - ^ =) with a length cap, keep it anchored, and keep it SSRF-safe since the symbol is interpolated into an upstream URL (encodeURIComponent).

Abba.title: Emoji-to-icon sweep injected ${ic()} template placeholders into quoted (non-template) strings
Abba.symptom: After a scripted emoji to SVG icon sweep, some buttons/labels rendered the literal text '${ic(...)}' instead of an icon.
Abba.fix: Regex pass restricted to backtick strings, and a post-sweep grep for the literal '${ic(' inside non-template quotes; convert those strings to concatenation. Always grep for the injected token's literal form after a mass replace.

Abba.title: Live chart watch board always fetched 1d candles even while the user was sharing a 1m chart
Abba.symptom: Watching a fast timeframe on TradingView, the board still read daily bars, so signal readouts did not match what the user saw.
Abba.fix: Added a timeframe selector (1m to 1d) to the board, stored it on the LW state, fetched at the chosen timeframe, and made Ava suggest switching the board and the TradingView chart when the top rule needs a different interval; verified the switch does not stop the screen-share stream.

Abba.title: Live-session P&L ignored the futures contract point value
Abba.symptom: NQ session P&L was computed with the wrong per-point value ($50 per point) instead of the contract point value, so futures trades in the live session summary were mis-valued.
Abba.fix: Exposed window.pointValue from views.js and used it in the session buildTradeBody; verified NQ and equity point values (equity x1) before committing.

Abba.title: Live-session voice parser took filler words as tickers and let exit/stop chunks overwrite the entry price
Abba.symptom: 'took profit exit at 18475' created symbol TOOK and overwrote NQ; the exit chunk's 'at 18475' replaced the entry price, so the saved trade lost its entry.
Abba.fix: Added the missing words to the keyword list, a guard that stops later chunks overwriting an established symbol, and made lifecycle chunks merge only close-side fields (exit_price, stop_price, target_price, pnl, fees); NQ entry 18450 to exit 18475 preserved.

Abba.title: Native media URL hardcoded to production ignored the API base, so lesson and strategy screenshots showed grey placeholders against a local dev API
Abba.symptom: On the simulator pointed at a local wrangler dev (ABBA_BASE), lesson screenshots stayed placeholders although curl to the same /api/media/<key> returned 200 image/png; a grep afterwards found DashboardView.swift:274 still hardcoded as well.
Abba.fix: mediaURL now returns base.absoluteString + '/media/' + key and the remaining hardcoded builder was found by grep and routed through it; verified on the simulator.

Abba.title: Naturally dictated trade phrasing ('log a trade, pinterest ticker PINS ... price right now is 23.47') logged nothing
Abba.symptom: A real user dictation with a company name, the word 'ticker' and a spoken price produced no trade at all.
Abba.fix: Added a ticker-phrase regex, a company-name to ticker map, a price-phrase regex and broader trade-intent detection; the exact failing utterance now yields {symbol: PINS, entry_price: 23.47}.

Abba.title: SQLite datetime('now') strings failed both ISO-8601 parsers on native, so events showed as 56 years old
